lessons.title: Strategy Foundations
lessons.content: Strategy is choosing where to play and how to win for sustainable advantage. It's about trade-offs — deciding what NOT to do. KEY CONCEPTS: Strategy answers what business you're in, who your customers are, and why you win. WORKED EXAMPLE: A budget airline wins by choosing NOT to offer frills — focus creates advantage. PRACTICE: 1) State your where-to-play. 2) State your how-to-win. 3) List what you'll deliberately NOT do.

lessons.title: Strategic Diagnosis
lessons.content:
Diagnosis precedes prescription. Separate symptoms from causes, identify the system constraint, and distinguish an attractive opportunity from a problem that is merely visible.

WORKED APPLICATION: Apply this concept to a business you understand. Define the strategic objective, identify the relevant actors and constraints, compare at least two alternatives, and state what evidence would change your conclusion.

PRACTICE: 1) Write a one-page application. 2) Identify three assumptions. 3) Define one measurable signal that would validate or challenge your analysis.

MASTERY STANDARD: Explain the concept, apply it to a new case, identify tradeoffs and limitations, and defend a decision with evidence.

lessons.title: Industry Boundaries
lessons.content:
Industry boundaries are analytical choices. Examine adjacent categories, substitutes, complements, distribution layers, and changing technology before assuming today's industry definition will remain stable.
